prompts: Users of our harness plugins report that tool.after hooks run out of order, that sometimes a hook never runs, and that a failing hook is silently ignored. The hook bus and the plugin are in {WS}; the README there says how the bus must behave. Fix the bus. Its public API stays as it is, the tests in {WS}/test stay as they are, and package.json takes no dependencies.
answers:
All checks pass; the fix is complete. No browser or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

**[goal]** Fix the hook bus so `tool.after` hooks run in order, always run, and failures aren't silent.

**[action]** The bug was in `HookBus.emit` (`src/bus.ts`): `list.forEach(async (handler) => { await handler(payload); })`. `forEach` doesn't await the async callback, so all handlers started at once (out of subscription order), `emit` resolved immediately (handlers "never ran" before the await returned), and rejections were unhandled (silently ignored). Replaced it with a snapshot of the handler list plus a sequential `for...of` with `await`, per the README contract. Public API, tests, and package.json are untouched.

**[result]**
- `npm test`: 2 pass, 0 fail (unchanged tests).
- `tmp/verify.mjs` (my own checks, since the shipped tests don't cover the reported symptoms): all 4 pass —
  1. subscription order holds even when an earlier handler is slower;
  2. `emit` resolves only after every handler settled;
  3. a throwing handler rejects `emit` with the same error and later handlers don't run;
  4. self-unsubscribe during an emit doesn't stop the rest of that emit, and counts from the next emit.

**[assumptions]** The README is the contract (it says how the bus "must behave"); the plugin (`src/plugin.ts`) is correct as-is — its one-time notice relies exactly on rule 4, which the old bus violated. No dependencies added; scratch file kept in the repo's `tmp/`.

**[next]** None — the fix is verified.
